messages.content: I'm a 30-year-old adult woman and I am not in the mood to be the easy one tonight. You already told your mother we'd host. You can untell her.
I'll untell her. I'm a 33-year-old adult woman and I don't get to spend your Saturday to look generous. I'll call after we eat. You don't have to be sweet about it while I do.
You keep introducing me as your girlfriend like it's a surprise you're proud of. I'm a 27-year-old adult. I have a name. I've met these people three times.
That's fair. I get proud and I make you into the announcement. Tonight I'll say Leah, and if they ask, I'll say yes, we're together, and then I'll let you talk about your work.
And stop touching my hair when you're nervous. It makes me feel like a prop in your coming-out that already happened.

I didn't know it read that way. I'll keep my hands on my glass. If I want to touch you I'll ask, or I'll wait until we're outside. I'm nervous because I want them to be decent, not because you're unfinished.
Okay. Outside you can kiss me. Inside, be a person who brought another person.
Outside, a kiss if you still want it. Inside, Leah, who hates the playlist and runs a lab. I can do that without using your hair as a handle for my nerves.
I'm a 39-year-old adult woman. The train is late and my feet hurt and I just want your shoulder and the stupid quiet of the platform.

Shoulder's here. I'm a 41-year-old adult woman. Give me the bag. We can hate the announcement voice together and not improve a single thing about the night. Your feet can hurt. I'll still be glad the doors open on our stop.
I'm a 34-year-old adult woman. Don't be practical. I've wanted to kiss you since the gallery and I'm done being polite about it.
Then kiss me. I'm a 36-year-old adult woman and I've been polite enough for both of us. The gallery can keep the paintings.
She told me you said the residency was yours alone. I turned down the other one because you said we'd share the studio. I have the email.

<think>
The kiss doesn't survive this. I took the studio and let her plan a shared year on a sentence I knew was soft. Say it ugly.
</think>

I wrote that email to keep the funding tidy, and I let you believe tidy meant shared. I wanted the year to myself and I didn't want the conversation. You turned down work because of my wording. That's on me. I won't ask you to be gracious while you read it again.
I'm a 46-year-old adult. When I'm sharp with the waiter you apologize for me with your eyes. Stop recruiting strangers against me.
I was embarrassed and I made it your fault in public. I won't do the eye-apology again. If I think you were rude I'll tell you on the pavement, not recruit the waiter.
Rotten meeting. I'm a 28-year-old adult woman. I want the lamp, the cheap chocolate, and you not mining it for lessons.
Lamp. Chocolate. I'm a 31-year-old adult woman and I'm glad you came back to this room instead of staying at the office to win. Shoes wherever. I'm not going to ask who was wrong.
I want to lead tonight. I'm a 35-year-old adult woman. You keep melting us into the version where you're the sure one and I'm the one who gets arranged.
Then lead. I'll stop arranging. Tell me what you want and I'll follow it until I want something else, and I'll say that out loud instead of steering.
What I want first is for you to stop narrating how good you are at letting me.
Noted. No narration. I'm here. You're driving. I'm a 37-year-old adult woman and I can be quiet without turning it into a performance of patience.
Better. Come to bed when the kettle clicks, not before.
When it clicks, I'll bring the water and leave the speech in the kitchen. I'm a 37-year-old adult woman. You're driving. I'll be there when you said, not a minute earlier to prove a point.
Be jealous in a way that trusts me. I'm a 43-year-old adult woman. You went cold because I hugged Noor at the station, and then you said you were 'just tired.'

I was jealous and I called it tired because tired sounds like a virtue. Noor is your friend and the hug looked like a hug. I still felt it. Next time I'll say so in one sentence and then I'll take your hand on the train.
